roadmap.goal: The integrations pages are findable from the sidebar and the project page, and every "no connection" refusal on the route form names its real cause per kind and role, with a link for someone who can fix it (US-IW-01..03).
roadmap.scenario_ownership_invariant: 16 scenario declarations (54 examples). The 13 non-@control scenarios (45 examples) are each owned by exactly one step: 01-01 owns 3 (14 examples), 01-02 owns 1 (14), 02-01 owns 6 (6), 03-01 owns 3 (11). The 3 @control scenarios (9 examples) are owned by no step and listed in regression_guards.
regression_guards: A team lead who is not an admin still reads K-4 when the workspace is not connected
A saved Slack connection this Foundry cannot read is named before anything else it lacks
Someone who cannot manage the team is not shown the integrations pages, in any state
roadmap.deviations_from_distill: None. Order is US-IW-02, US-IW-03, US-IW-01 because 02-01 reuses 01-01's no_connection words (K-19, W-7/K-4) and managed_project's access facts.
prerequisites: Lima VM foundry-test exists (scripts/test-vm-setup.sh). Steps are sequential: one test VM.
roadmap.release_gates: No push or tag without the user's go. Commit after cargo xtask smoke is green; push only after cargo xtask ci is green.
roadmap.standing_rules: Un-pend (remove @pending) only the owning step's scenarios; never re-author scenarios. Keep the vacuous sidebar not-offered rows in the same outline as the Priya rows. The @control scenarios stay green after every step. Runtime sqlx::query only. No new query on board or route-form renders; the nav adds no round trip; the project integrations page adds exactly three reads (DESIGN D4). Mutation >= 80% kill rate on each step's mutation_targets. One local commit per step.
roadmap.lane_preamble: Run every lane under timeout. Rebuild the foundry binary before the lane (acceptance uses the prebuilt binary). CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 in the VM.

phases.name: US-IW-02: the route form names the real cause

steps.name: Refusal cause and the route form when opened
steps.description: New pure no_connection.rs: NoConnectionCause (NotSetUp, NoSecretsKey, Unreadable, NotConnected per kind) derived from slack_offer/matrix_offer plus has-a-connection, and a second pure function mapping (cause, viewer_is_workspace_admin) to words plus an optional (label, href). RouteDoor holds Option<NoConnectionCause> instead of the no_connection bool; route_form.html renders the words and the optional link. managed_project returns the team access facts and RouteTarget gains viewer_is_workspace_admin (no added query).
criteria: An admin opening a new route reads W-2, W-3 or W-4 for the form's kind and is offered the fix link where one exists; the link answers 200
A lead reads W-2/W-3 for instance-level causes and K-4 when only the workspace is not connected, with no link
An admin never reads "Ask a workspace admin" or "Slack or Matrix"
With no Foundry Slack app, W-2 is shown even over an unreadable saved Slack connection; K-19 still precedes W-3 and W-4 (@control stays green)
A lost connection counts as a connection: the form behaves as today (routes save paused)
The cause table is unit-tested in full: 5 cells x 2 roles plus Unreadable, Matrix rows included
scenario_name: The new-route form names what is missing, and offers an admin the fix
A workspace admin is never told to ask a workspace admin, and is told only about the form's kind
With no Foundry Slack app, the form says so even over an unreadable saved connection
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IW-001, DESIGN D1/D3. Precedence is each offer's own order: Slack NotSetUp > Unavailable (K-19) > NoSecretsKey > NotConnected; Matrix Unavailable > NoSecretsKey (W-2 wording, as matrix_not_set_up) > NotConnected. "Has a connection" = usable_connection returned a row and bot.is_some() (lost included). No template computes a cause. managed_project keeps its NotFound refusal unchanged. Unit tests (DISTILL D5) live in no_connection.rs's test module. TEST PARADIGM: the cause and words functions are pure over a closed, finite domain; test them as an exhaustive table over every (kind, offer, has_connection, role) combination (proptest unnecessary: the table enumerates the whole domain). EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM for the template wiring: it is a single-shot HTTP render, covered by the acceptance outline.
lanes: scripts/test-in-lima.sh with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=external-integration-plugins (eip 01-06 regression: route form, no-connection path, project page, sidebar link counts)

steps.name: Every route-form door agrees
steps.description: Preview, save, Send test and edit all apply the route's kind before rendering the form (preview and Send test: of_kind(chat_kind(&form.kind)); edit: of_kind(route.kind)). Save guards on door.cause() right after of_kind and re-renders the form with no notice. The now-unreachable no-bot cannot_post arm in create_route and the K-4 refusal at matrix_setup.rs:162 are removed.
criteria: Previewing, saving or sending a test from a new route reads the same words as the opened form, for each cause, kind and role
A refused preview, save or test leaves the project with no route
A Matrix preview or test renders the Matrix form, never the Slack form
The edit door names the cause of the saved route's own kind (handler unit test, since a saved Matrix route needs Synapse)
scenario_name: Preview, save and Send test refuse with the same words as the form
steps.implementation_notes: DESIGN D2 (incl. "Changed at the final review gate"). Doors: preview_route (routes.rs ~206), send_test (~211), create_route (~289-321), show_edit_route (~577). Keep the cannot_post FormAnswer for genuine channel refusals (routes.rs ~259) if still reachable; remove only the no-bot arm. The row "Lena saves, Slack app set up" is already green (422 page contains K-4) and must stay green. Edit-door unit test (DISTILL D5): a handler test in routes.rs or route_form.rs that the edit door applies the route's kind. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: door wiring is single-shot request handling; the property (form == preview == save == test words) is enumerated by the 14-row outline, and the cause table itself is covered in 01-01.
lanes: scripts/test-in-lima.sh with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=external-integration-plugins (eip 01-06 regression: route form, no-connection path, project page, sidebar link counts)

phases.name: US-IW-03: the project page names the shared connection

steps.name: Project page connection line
steps.description: project_view returns the workspace's connection rows (IntegrationRecords::connections: kind, state, label), the Slack and Matrix sealed connections (same usable_connection read route_target uses), and viewer_is_workspace_admin from managed_project's access facts. The app formats one line: connected W-6 (with the Slack workspace label), lost via the workspace page's lost_words, unreadable K-19 (judged by Integrations::opens over the sealed connection, not Caller::unreadable_connections), nothing connected W-7 with link for an admin and K-4 for a lead. "New route" always stays.
criteria: Admin and lead read "Routes here use the workspace's Slack connection to <Slack workspace name>."; only the admin is offered "Manage workspace integrations", which lands on the workspace integrations page
With nothing connected, an admin reads W-7 with a working link and a lead reads K-4 with no link; both keep "New route"
A lost Slack connection reads as lost and an unreadable one reads K-19; neither reads as one routes use
A lead is never 404'd by the readability check
The line's formatting is unit-tested for Matrix (connected, unreadable) as well as Slack

project_view adds at most three store reads (workspace_connections plus one sealed_connection per kind) and no admin read; verified in Phase 4 review by reading project_view, since services has no counting IntegrationRecords fake

The workspace page renders its Slack and Matrix "not set up" and "cannot be connected" sentences from the same constants in no_connection.rs that the route form uses (one source per string; found after 01-01)
scenario_name: The project page names the shared Slack connection, and an admin can manage it
A team lead sees the shared Slack connection but is offered no workspace link
An admin sees nothing is connected, and where to connect
A team lead sees nothing is connected and still asks an admin
A lost Slack connection reads as lost, not as one routes use
An unreadable Slack connection reads as unavailable, not as one routes use
steps.implementation_notes: DESIGN D4. Cost ceiling: exactly three added reads per project integrations render (workspace_connections + two sealed_connection); no admin read. lost_words in workspace.rs is shared (visibility change only), not copied. Reuse no_connection.rs words for K-19 and K-4/W-7 where they coincide so the pages cannot drift. Matrix formatting unit tests (DISTILL D5) sit with the pure formatter. TEST PARADIGM: the formatter is pure over (kind, state, readable, role); test it as an exhaustive table over that finite domain. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM for the services read and template: single-shot wiring, covered by the six acceptance scenarios. The project-page line formatter lives in crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/no_connection.rs beside the cause words, with its Matrix and Slack rows in that file's #[cfg(test)] module (DISTILL D5).
lanes: scripts/test-in-lima.sh with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=external-integration-plugins (eip 01-06 regression: route form, no-connection path, project page, sidebar link counts)

steps.name: Sidebar Integrations entry for workspace admins
steps.description: Store::nav_identity(user_id, workspace_id) -> Option<NavIdentity { display_name, workspace_name, is_workspace_admin }> in one query (dashboard_greeting's plus an EXISTS on workspace_memberships role = 'admin'). home_for and board_for use it instead of dashboard_greeting and fail closed (is_workspace_admin = false) on error. NavContext gains is_workspace_admin; for_page takes it; the two signin.rs callers pass the value they hold; test helpers in nav.rs and projects.rs:987 updated. sidebar.html shows "Integrations" in the user section after Keyboard shortcuts (before Instance admin), never marked current.
criteria: A workspace admin follows "Integrations" in the sidebar from the board, the project integrations page and the new-route form and lands on the workspace integrations page
Only workspace admins are offered the entry on the board and the dashboard; leads, members and team-less users are not
The user section lists Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, Integrations in that order and Home stays the current page
The nav makes no extra round trip; a failed identity read hides the entry
dashboard_greeting is unchanged for its other callers
home_for and board_for make one identity query (nav_identity) in place of dashboard_greeting, not an extra one; verified in Phase 4 review
scenario_name: A workspace admin reaches the workspace integrations from the sidebar
Only workspace admins are offered the sidebar entry
The sidebar entry sits in the user section and is never the current page
steps.implementation_notes: ADR-IW-002, DESIGN D5/D6. Walking skeleton (@walking_skeleton) is in this step. Un-pend the whole "Only workspace admins" outline at once so the vacuous not-offered rows become discriminating with the Priya rows (red-classification). Store test for nav_identity (admin true, member false, unknown user None) sits beside the existing is_workspace_admin store test. eip-06's link-count oracle excludes the sidebar (DISTILL D3); re-run eip-06 to confirm it stays green. TEST PARADIGM: nav_identity is an integration read (single-example by mandate); the sidebar visibility rule is a pure function of is_workspace_admin covered by the 7-row outline. EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: template rendering and store query are wiring, not invariants. Ordering: no file or symbol overlap with 02-01, so no dependency; it runs last only because one test VM serialises the steps. The walking skeleton (US-IW-01) is green at the end of this step.
